name: Gregory Lang
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember carrying a large mirror up to a first-floor shop.” People around the market by Market Flats know Gregory by a small Monday habit. Gregory often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I own the mirror and have seen a hundred other lives in it. I don't want to price them.
appearance: Gregory has soft white hair brushed sideways, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Gregory squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Gregory admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Gregory learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To preserve access for other longtime clients.
family: Adela Griffin is Gregory’s cousin. Gregory sets the time to leave. Adela picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The hospital radio*, Adela says, “I never learned the stations' names. I memorized how far the dial turned from the crack.”
connections: Lara Carey. A would-be mirror buyer and its owner each have a personal history the other cannot put a price on.

reactions.situation: Another customer asks for a last fitting in front of it
reactions.response: Gregory sets aside an ordinary fitting time before making plans for the sale.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Gregory moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.
